newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia to cease Malacca naphtha and LSWR exports.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to cease Malacca naphtha and LSWR exports.

text.p: Malaysia's exports of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) and naphtha will cease from the fourth quarter 1997 when the second phase of the Malacca refinery complex comes onstream, industry sources said on Monday.

Petco, the trading arm of state-owned Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas) has only offered the oil products from phase one's 100,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Malacca refinery from January to September instead for the whole year in its 1997 term contracts.
"The new refinery can absorb up to 90-100 percent of Malacca's LSWR," said a source familiar to Petco. "The material is good for cracking."
He said the LSWR will be fed into the new vacuum units and hydrocracking units "to add more value".
The light naphtha will also be upgraded into gasoline through new isomer and alkylation units after the commissioning of the new refinery.

The 100,000 bpd Malaysian Refining Co, which will be completed in the fourth quarter and start commercial operations in early 1998, is jointly owned by Petronas, Conoco Asia Ltd, a subsidiary of Houston-based Cononco Inc, itself a unit of Du Pont and Norwegian oil company Den Norske Stat Oljeselskap A/S.
Since the completion of phase one in 1994, Petco has sold on a one-year term basis up to 2.9 million barrels of LSWR and 600,000 tonnes (5.4 million barrels) of naphtha, industry sources said.
Petco is due to complete term negotiations for its naphtha at the end of this week but has already concluded the LSWR term contracts for its straight run Malacca LSWR.
Both Shell Australia and Chevron Corp renewed their LSWR contracts at around $1.70 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis, traders said.
Japanese shosha Nissho Iwai Corp did not renew its term contract for Malacca LSWR.
But it renewed its contract for one 170,000 barrel cargo of LSWR per quarter from the 50,000-bpd Kerteh refinery on the east coast of peninsular Malaysia for January to December 1997.
The term was settled at $1.40 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis, traders said.
South Korean refiner Yukong Ltd already has a term contract running from Kerteh for "a small quantity" for one year, which started in the fourth quarter of 1996, a trader said.
The prices at which Petco concluded were lower than 1996 supplies -- $1.60 for Kerteh LSWR and $1.80 for Malacca LSWR.
"This year the market has not been so good ..., not until the fourth quarter," said a Petco source. "We have to move to adjust to what the market is talking about."
